proofs.proof_tex:
The first assertion is exactly the counterexample established by \(\mathrm{thm:generated\text{-}prefix\text{-}coupling}\).  To spell out why it rules out the asserted all-prefix approximation, let \(k_n\) be the deterministic interior prefix supplied there.  Any coupling satisfying
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left|
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n-b_{n,k}\}-G_{n,k}
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1) \tag{1}
\]
would, by retaining the single term indexed by \(k_n\), imply
\[
 \left|
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}-G_{n,k_n}
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{2}
\]
But the cited core theorem proves that the statistic on the left of (2) before subtraction has a subsequential limit \(Z+H(X)\), where \(Z\) is Gaussian, \(H(X)\) is bounded, nonconstant, and independent of \(Z\), and \(Z+H(X)\) is non-Gaussian.  In contrast, every coordinate of every centered Gaussian process is Gaussian.  Equation (2) would force the two marginal laws to have bounded-Lipschitz distance tending to zero: for every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one,
\[
 \left|E f(S_n)-E f(G_{n,k_n})\right|
 \le E\min\{2,|S_n-G_{n,k_n}|\}\longrightarrow0, \tag{3}
\]
where \(S_n=\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}\).  The convergence in (3) follows because, for each \(u>0\),
\[
 E\min\{2,|S_n-G_{n,k_n}|\}
 \le u+2\mathbb P_n\{|S_n-G_{n,k_n}|>u\},
\]
and (2) makes the probability tend to zero, after which \(u\downarrow0\).  This contradicts the proved non-Gaussian subsequential limit.  Therefore (1) fails.  More generally, suppose a covariance-only repair coupled \(S_n\) within \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) of a centered Gaussian variable with variance \(v_n\).  Along the counterexample's convergent subsequence, tightness of \(S_n\) and the coupling would make those Gaussian variables tight.  A centered normal family is tight only if \(v_n\) is bounded; after passage to a further subsequence, \(v_n\to v\ge0\), so the Gaussian variables converge to \(N(0,v)\).  The coupling would then make the same subsequence of \(S_n\) converge to \(N(0,v)\), contradicting its non-Gaussian limit.  Thus changing only a covariance matrix cannot repair the coordinate.  The counterexample's omitted term is the empirical fixed-cardinality quantile-boundary term, so the obstruction is a distributional boundary correction, not merely a covariance correction.

For the second assertion, apply \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}support\text{-}tie\text{-}witness}\) under its displayed feasibility conditions.  That theorem establishes membership of its construction in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) and, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)^2
 \ge B_n^2(a_n^{\dagger})^2
 \longrightarrow D_\infty>0. \tag{4}
\]
Taking square roots in (4), justified because all terms are nonnegative, gives
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)
 \ge \sqrt{D_\infty}>0. \tag{5}
\]
The same theorem applies the definition of the sharp modulus to the exact equalities in (4) and proves
\[
 \omega^{\star}(0)\ge\sqrt{D_\infty}>0. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (1)--(3) prove failure of the frozen Gaussian all-prefix coupling, while (4)--(6) prove failure of exact leading-MSE tie invariance.  These are precisely the two conclusions in the corrected statement.

added_lemmas.statement:
On a joint probability space carrying the observed sample and \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\), suppose there is a deterministic sequence \(a_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
 \left|
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,k}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})
 \right|=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1), \tag{7}
\]
and, on defining
\[
 R_n=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}
       |\widehat C_{n,k}-Q_{n,k}(G_n)|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M_n(a)=
 \left\{k\in\mathcal K_n:
 Q_{n,k}(G_n)\le
 \min_{j\in\mathcal K_n}Q_{n,j}(G_n)+2a
 \right\},
\]
\[
 D_n(a)=\max_{k,l\in\mathcal M_n(a)}d_n(k,l),
\]
one has
\[
 \mathbb P_n(R_n\le a_n)\to1,
 \qquad
 D_n(a_n)\sqrt{\log(e|\mathcal K_n|)}
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{8}
\]
Then the bounded-Lipschitz distance between the law of
\(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\) and the law of
\(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)}\) tends to zero.  This is a conditional transfer result only: it does not assert that (7)--(8) hold for the generated fixed-cardinality prefix estimator.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(J_n=J_n(G_n)\).  On the event \(\{R_n\le a_n\}\), optimality of \(\widehat k_n\) for \(\widehat C_n\) and of \(J_n\) for \(Q_n(G_n)\) gives, equation by equation,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q_{n,\widehat k_n}(G_n)
 &\le \widehat C_{n,\widehat k_n}+a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(R_n\)},\\
 &\le \widehat C_{n,J_n}+a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(\widehat k_n\)},\\
 &\le Q_{n,J_n}(G_n)+2a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(R_n\)},\\
 &=\min_{j\in\mathcal K_n}Q_{n,j}(G_n)+2a_n
 &&\text{by the definition of \(J_n\)}.
 \end{aligned} \tag{9}
\]
Thus \(\widehat k_n\in\mathcal M_n(a_n)\); also \(J_n\in\mathcal M_n(a_n)\) directly from the definition of that set.  Consequently,
\[
 d_n(\widehat k_n,J_n)\le D_n(a_n) \tag{10}
\]
on \(\{R_n\le a_n\}\).

For deterministic \(k,l\in\mathcal K_n\), the definition of \(d_n\) yields
\[
 |\beta_{n,k}-\beta_{n,l}|\le d_n(k,l),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l})
 \le d_n(k,l)^2. \tag{11}
\]
The second inequality remains valid when \(\Gamma_n\) is singular.  Let \(m_n=|\mathcal K_n|\).  If \(d_n(k,l)\le r\) for \(r>0\), the centered Gaussian variable \(G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}\) has variance at most \(r^2\).  Its moment-generating function is therefore bounded by \(\exp(t^2r^2/2)\).  For \(u>0\), Markov's inequality gives the upper-tail bound \(\exp\{-tu+t^2r^2/2\}\); minimizing over \(t>0\) at \(t=u/r^2\), and applying the same argument to the lower tail, gives
\[
 \mathbb P\{|G_{n,k}-G_{n,l}|>u\}
 \le 2\exp\{-u^2/(2r^2)\}. \tag{12}
\]
There are at most \(m_n^2\) ordered pairs.  By (11), (12), and the union bound, for every \(x>0\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb P\Bigg[
 \max_{\substack{k,l\in\mathcal K_n\\d_n(k,l)\le r}}
 |(\beta_{n,k}+G_{n,k})-(\beta_{n,l}+G_{n,l})|\\
 >r+r\sqrt{2\{\log(2m_n^2)+x\}}
 \Bigg]\le e^{-x}. 
 \end{split} \tag{13}
\]

Let \(L_n=\log(em_n)\).  The second condition in (8) says that
\(D_n(a_n)\sqrt{L_n}=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\).  Hence there exists a deterministic sequence \(c_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)\sqrt{L_n}>c_n\}\to0. \tag{14}
\]
For completeness, choose successively deterministic thresholds \(c_n\) decreasing to zero along indices after which the probability of exceeding the current threshold is at most that threshold; this diagonal construction proves (14) directly from convergence in probability.  Set \(r_n=c_n/\sqrt{L_n}\).  Then
\[
 \mathbb P_n\{D_n(a_n)>r_n\}\to0,
 \qquad
 r_n\sqrt{L_n}=c_n\to0. \tag{15}
\]
Apply (13) with \(r=r_n\).  Since \(\log(2m_n^2)\le 2L_n+\log2\), equations (10), (13), and (15), together with \(\mathbb P_n(R_n\le a_n)\to1\), imply
\[
 (\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 -(\beta_{n,J_n}+G_{n,J_n})=o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{16}
\]

Evaluating the maximum in (7) at the data-dependent index \(\widehat k_n\) gives
\[
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,\widehat k_n}+G_{n,\widehat k_n})
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{17}
\]
Combining (16) and (17),
\[
 \Delta_n:=
 \sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)
 -(\beta_{n,J_n(G_n)}+G_{n,J_n(G_n)})
 =o_{\mathbb P_n}(1). \tag{18}
\]
For every real function \(f\) bounded by one and with Lipschitz constant at most one,
\[
 \left|E f(X_n)-E f(Y_n)\right|
 \le E\min\{2,|\Delta_n|\}, \tag{19}
\]
where \(X_n\) and \(Y_n\) are the two variables in (18).  For every \(u>0\), the right side of (19) is at most
\[
 u+2\mathbb P_n(|\Delta_n|>u),
\]
which tends to at most \(u\) by (18), and then to zero as \(u\downarrow0\).  Taking the supremum over the bounded-Lipschitz class proves the asserted convergence of laws.
added_lemmas.justification: This lemma isolates the valid deterministic selection-transfer argument from the invalid claim that the frozen Gaussian coupling holds for generated fixed-cardinality prefixes.
added_lemmas.gap: It is an internal transfer lemma, not a claimed extension of a published fixed-prefix theorem.
added_lemmas.consumer: Any future rank-boundary-corrected joint process can use this lemma after its primitive approximation and near-minimizer stability conditions are proved.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The frozen Gaussian quadratic local-gap law is not valid on the displayed classes.  First, for an admissible choice of the fixed constants there exist a sequence \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P^{\mathrm{reg}}\) and an interior deterministic prefix \(k_n/n_{\mathcal E}\to 1/2\) for which
\[
 \sqrt n\{\widehat\tau_{n,k_n}-\tau_n-b_{n,k_n}\}
\]
has a non-Gaussian subsequential limit.  Hence the asserted all-prefix \(o_{\mathbb P_n}(1)\) coupling to \(G_n\sim N(0,\Gamma_n)\) fails, and replacing \(\Gamma_n\) by another covariance matrix cannot by itself repair that coordinate.  Second, whenever the feasibility conditions of \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}support\text{-}tie\text{-}witness}\) hold, there is a sequence in \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{legal}}\) and prefixes \(k_n^{\dagger}\) and \(0\) such that, for every sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \rho_{n,k_n^{\dagger}}=\rho_{n,0},
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}d_n(k_n^{\dagger},0)>0,
 \qquad
 \omega^{\star}(0)>0.
\]
Thus neither the frozen Gaussian all-prefix coupling nor exact leading-MSE tie invariance is available from the stated primitive conditions.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old universal Gaussian-quadratic conclusion is false: the established regular-class fixed-cardinality counterexample has a non-Gaussian boundary limit, and the established legal-class witness has an exact leading-MSE tie with separated ATE coordinates.  The proposed claim removes the invalid positive assertion and retains only the rigorously established negative boundary.

proposed.gap: Published fixed-prefix and given-ranking results do not cover the empirical rank-boundary process or tie-uniform selection.
proposed.consumer: This obstruction determines what must be repaired before a selected-ATE limit law or multiplier interval can be certified.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed negative claim uses the two established counterexample theorems and no longer depends on the invalid unconditional quadratic selector representation.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: The causal estimand remains \(\tau_n=E_{P_n}[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid R=1]\), and the displayed prefix estimators and selector remain sample maps aimed at that estimand.  The current core does not establish an unconditional weak law for \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{n,\widehat k_n}-\tau_n)\).  The conditional quadratic transfer lemma yields such a bounded-Lipschitz conclusion only after a valid rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator/criterion approximation and quantitative near-minimizer stability have been proved.  The established counterexample shows that the frozen \(\Gamma_n\) process does not supply this approximation and that, on the present regular class, the missing fixed-cardinality boundary term may be non-Gaussian.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous metadata still displayed a Gaussian-quadratic selected law as the operative functional.  The corrected metadata distinguishes the causal target from the presently unproved selected-estimator limit and records the non-Gaussian boundary obstruction.

proposed.comparator_claim: Theorem~2 gives \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) MSE estimation for any given borrowed set, and Theorem~3 gives selection consistency for a given influence ranking under a fixed positive separation.
Theorem~1 gives asymptotic normality of a fixed-prefix estimator after centering by its prefix-specific bias.
Theorems~2.3 and~3.1 show local nonuniform impossibility for estimating post-model-selection distributions in broad nested and AIC-like selection problems.
Theorem~3 derives a local focused-selection law and Theorem~4 guarantees coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\gamma\) for a fixed invalid-instrument selection problem.
Theorem~3.1 characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity by full differentiability under a Gaussian limit, and Theorem~3.2 validates derivative-aware resampling.
The sorting operator is Hadamard differentiable at regular values and yields a uniform sorted-process central limit theorem and bootstrap bands on compact interior quantile sets.
Theorems~2.1 and~2.6 give Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors under sub-exponential or polynomial moments.
Theorem~1 gives selective coverage by simultaneous inference over a data-dependent set of locally plausible targets.
Conditional truncated-Gaussian and hybrid projection procedures correct the winner's curse when a target coordinate is selected by optimizing noisy estimates.
Theorem~2.3 gives exact Fisher-randomization-test size under a sharp null, and Theorem~3.5 gives an excess-risk bound for an adaptive conformal borrowing threshold.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The project no longer claims a strict simultaneous strengthening of Yang--Li--Wu--Yang.  Its proved relation to those fixed-prefix results is a non-representability boundary for the attempted frozen-covariance extension.

prose_updates.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing is a focused selection problem with a generated, fixed-cardinality ranking and a squared estimated-bias criterion.  The proved boundary is negative: even on the regular continuous-score class, the frozen fixed-threshold influence process omits a first-order empirical rank-boundary term that can have a non-Gaussian limit, so neither the proposed all-prefix Gaussian coupling nor its unconditional quadratic selected-ATE law is valid.  Separately, a bounded no-covariate squared-loss construction gives legal nested prefixes with exactly equal leading MSE but separated root-\(n\) ATE coordinates, and hence \(\omega^{\star}(0)>0\).  A proved conditional transfer lemma explains how a corrected joint process would yield a selected law, but deriving that rank-corrected process and primitive near-minimizer control, the sharp excess modulus, and a valid multiplier interval remain open.

project_justification.fill: The project establishes a non-representability boundary for the attempted frozen-covariance all-prefix extension, proves a legal exact-risk-tie counterexample with positive ATE-coordinate separation, and isolates a rigorous conditional near-minimizer transfer lemma.  It does not claim an unconditional quadratic law for the generated selector: the remaining proof obligation is to derive the rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator/criterion process from primitive conditions, allowing a non-Gaussian boundary process on the current class, together with sufficient near-minimizer or entropy control before constructing tie-uniform inference.

prose_updates.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the influence score in equation~(3), the nested top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1, fixed-prefix bias and Gaussian behavior in Theorem~1, pointwise MSE estimation in Theorem~2, and given-ranking fixed-gap selection consistency in Theorem~3.  The present counterexample shows that these results do not extend to the generated fixed-cardinality all-prefix path by using the frozen fixed-threshold covariance \(\Gamma_n\): the empirical quantile boundary contributes at first order and can be non-Gaussian.  Claeskens and Hjort supply the local-misspecification and focused-risk architecture, including the non-estimability of local bias.  Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess derive focused-selector inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem, but their candidate list is not generated by estimated individual ranks.  Leeb and Poetscher provide the generic local nonuniformity background for selection.  Fang and Santos explain why ordinary resampling can fail at nondifferentiable maps and motivate derivative-aware resampling.  Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo derive regular-value sorting derivatives, but the present class does not impose the score-index smoothness needed to turn every rank-boundary contribution into a Gaussian linear correction.  Chernozhukov and coauthors provide orthogonal fixed-target expansions, and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike provide Gaussian and multiplier approximations for high-dimensional sample-mean vectors; neither result removes the need to derive the correct ranked functional first.  Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen, Zrnic and Fithian, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey provide localization or optimization-selection architectures that become relevant only after that process is identified.  Zhu, Yang, and Wang study exact sharp-null randomization validity and conformal threshold borrowing, not a superpopulation weak-null ATE interval for this generated influence-ranked selector.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The local-risk coordinate is the \(n\)-scaled MSE under \(n^{-1/2}\) exchangeability violations.  The legal exact-tie witness may contain score atoms and therefore need not lie in the regular margin class.  The separate coupling counterexample does lie in the regular class and has a continuous score, but its score-indexed outcome oscillates at the empirical rank-boundary scale; the resulting fixed-cardinality boundary term is non-Gaussian.  Thus a density margin alone is insufficient.  A positive selected-law theorem needs a primitive linearization of both the external empirical quantile boundary and the trial-generated score perturbation, plus smoothness or other structure controlling score-indexed conditional contributions and quantitative stability of random near minimizers.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established headline is the negative boundary: the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian all-prefix coupling fails for a regular continuous-score sequence, and exact leading-MSE ties can have nonvanishing ATE-coordinate distance on the broader legal class.  The conditional quadratic transfer lemma is proved, but it is not an achievability theorem for the actual generated selector.  The named remaining proof obligation is to derive from primitive conditions a rank-boundary-corrected joint estimator/criterion process, allowing a non-Gaussian boundary term on the current class unless additional score-index smoothness justifies a Gaussian correction, and to prove sufficient near-minimizer or entropy control.  The sharp excess modulus on restricted prefix-Gram subclasses and the computable tie-uniform multiplier interval remain open.  The fixed-gap and no-borrowing propositions remain conditional sanity checks and carry no generated-path novelty claim.

statement_notes.justification: The corrected headline records the two proved obstructions that prevent the frozen Gaussian quadratic law from describing the generated fixed-cardinality selector.
statement_notes.gap: Neither fixed-prefix theory nor a density margin accounts for the empirical rank-boundary contribution, and exact leading-risk ties do not force target-coordinate ties.
statement_notes.consumer: A valid selected-ATE law and multiplier interval must replace the frozen process and localize over target-stable near minimizers.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma preserves the valid selection-transfer argument without asserting that its coupling and stability hypotheses follow from the current generated-ranking class.
statement_notes.gap: The unresolved mathematical work lies in establishing the lemma's hypotheses for the rank-corrected process, not in the transfer inequality itself.
statement_notes.consumer: It will convert a future primitive rank-corrected process theorem into the corresponding selected-estimator bounded-Lipschitz law.
